[P2] Cover unreadable bodies on HTTP error responses

The interrupted-body test supplies HTTP 200, while every HTTP-error fixture has a readable body. Removing this `.catch()` therefore leaves the assertions unchanged. Without it, an interrupted HTTP 503 body would propagate a non-retryable `TypeError`, losing the status-based retry. This violates CONTRIBUTING rule 4. Return to the response-handling/test design and require unreadable 503 and 422 responses to retain their `DeciderError.status` and corresponding retry decisions, or consolidate the reading paths while preserving those outcomes.
